Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) to see if there are real or complex roots. If positive, two real solutions; if zero, one solution; if negative, two complex ones. To find stationary points, first take the derivative of f(x), denoted f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are potential stationary points. Plug them back into the original function to find the corresponding y-values. Then, use the second derivative test: if f''(x) > 0, it's a local minimum; if f''(x) < 0, a local maximum; if zero, it's inconclusive. This helps identify where the function changes direction.
